clue.text: What the poor do, having ill-fitting windows?

definitions.text: What the poor do, having ill-fitting windows?

parts.words: What the poor do, having ill-fitting windows?
parts.note: to be short of money is idiomatically to suffer a chill wind; the clue pretends this is literal, with cold air coming through badly fitted window frames

explanation.surface: A sympathetic thought about poor households shivering beside badly fitted windows.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase has two lives: hard-up people feel a financial pinch, and anyone with gaps round the window frames literally feels cold air blowing in.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to suffer from shortage of money, which is what the poor endure, and also literally to sense cold air.

clue.text: They're short-lived, coming from border in record time

clue.text: Put the men to work for such an unspecified time

clue.text: Be obliged to save energy and come to a standstill
